replaces.idea: A twin-roller conveyor bench with a continuous notched belt loop carrying crates, representing a shared paravirtualized virtqueue.
An upright accordion bellows pump with a pressure dial and pedal base, representing virtio-balloon memory reclamation.
A chunky upright ROM cartridge with a ribbed top grip on a bevelled base, representing virtual guest firmware.

new.name: Balloon Pump
new.depicts: An upright accordion bellows with a T-handle on top, a round pressure dial on its front plate, and a flat pedal base.
new.focal: the round pressure dial on the bellows

new.name: Ring Conveyor
new.depicts: A horizontal twin-roller conveyor bench on four short legs, with a continuous notched belt loop and two small crates riding on top.
new.focal: the notched belt loop between the two rollers

new.name: Boot Cartridge
new.depicts: A chunky upright ROM cartridge with a ribbed grip on top and a bevelled base plate.

new.name: Passthrough Coupler
new.depicts: A heavy flanged pipe coupling bolted to a floor bracket, with a straight brass conduit passing cleanly through its center.
new.focal: the straight conduit passing through the flanged collar

new.name: State Polaroid
new.depicts: A boxy instant camera resting on a squat tripod stand, with a thick square film card sticking out of its front slot.
new.focal: the square film card protruding from the front slot

new.name: Null-Modem Plug
new.depicts: A trapezoidal D-sub 9-pin connector housing standing on a small rubber boot, with two thumbscrews flanking its top.
new.focal: the twin thumbscrews on the D-sub housing

new.name: Watchdog Bell
new.depicts: A dome-shaped brass desk bell on a dark base with a tiny spring-loaded striker lever on its side.

rework.redesign: Redraw as a heavy industrial rack-mounted hypervisor cabinet on four leveling feet, with two recessed machine-bay doors and a physical teleprinter keyboard shelf below.
Redraw as a tiny winged visor-beetle with a rounded carapace and two 1x1 dark-ink eyes so its silhouette is distinct from c:ept:core.
